findings.description: Observed execution telemetry is overwritten or contaminated by scheduler metadata before certificate validation.
findings.fix: Select a consumer_observed execution mapping atomically from supported explicit telemetry locations; do not merge its scope or executed_horizon with RTC/adaptive scheduler mappings. Add regression cases for conflicting current response RTC and legacy RTC without an evidence_scope. Keep serving_only suppression.
findings.why: Reproduced on public17e: sample.action_execution={evidence_scope:consumer_observed,executed_horizon:2}, response.rtc={evidence_scope:runtime_schedule,planned_horizon:50,executed_horizon:50} yields runtime_schedule horizon50 then None, rejecting valid observed telemetry. More seriously, sample.action_execution={evidence_scope:consumer_observed} with legacy response.rtc={executed_horizon:50} yields consumer_observed horizon50 despite no consumer-observed horizon, defeating the new contract.

scope: Independent API, dependencies and evidence review of public17e and Studio dc5b18d4. Exact package markers and isolated CPU/GPU ORT selection inspected, setup hash/index contract and provider strictness/reporting inspected. Existing receipts reused. Actual GPU model qualification remains unknown and is not itself a source merge blocker.
